articles.title: Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce Hit With 'Catastrophic' Allegations 3 Months After Marriage
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s honeymoon stage may be over as their plans for their married life hit a major hurdle. Swift, 36, and Kelce, 37, who married t...
articles.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's honeymoon stage may be over as their plans for their married life hit a major hurdle.

Swift, 36, and Kelce, 37, who married three months ago in a July 3 ceremony at New York's Madison Square Garden, faced backlash from their Ohio neighbors at a village planning meeting on October 6, the Daily Mail reported on October 8.

The couple's plans to erect fencing and plant trees around their $5 million mansion in Bratenahl were the source of much strife at the meeting, with residents accusing the "absentee" couple of causing a "tremendous blow" to the community's "peace and quiet," according to transcripts obtained by the Daily Mail .

In September, the Bratenahl Architectural Review Board approved plans to build a 6-foot fence around the property, but neighbors raised concerns about the couple's landscaping plans during a Tuesday meeting.

Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door to the home Kelce and Swift bought in March for over three decades, predicted there would be "catastrophic sewer backups" if the couple planted evergreens near the old sewage line their properties share.

Bolton is allegedly discussing the dilemma with Swift and Kelce's attorney after she was quoted $75,000 to line the sewage system against roots. "This applicant may decide to sell her house next year, maybe move on and buy another house," Bolton said.

"What am I going to do when I have 50 evergreen trees on my sewer line, and they're gone?" she asked. "And I'm still living here in Bratenahl."

Another, Chuck Bauernschmidt, who lives two doors down from the A-listers, accused the pair of "ridiculous … clear-cutting of the shrubbery and everything else."

He claimed "all the trees are gone" and expressed concerns that deer could impale themselves on the planned fence.

Kelce and Swift's planner, Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction, defended his clients, explaining they were "looking for privacy and security … after one of the largest sales in Cuyahoga County." He also noted that the couple scaled back plans for an 8-foot fence to a shorter 6-foot fence that stops short of Lake Erie.

Kutz claimed they made changes "just to show that [they're] good neighbors," including having the sewage line jetted and cleaned "without asking for help" and adding a gate for Bauernschmidt, who felt "closed off."

A third plan for the property will be presented at a future meeting, but the board did approve the landscaping in front of the estate on Tuesday.

In September, after The Wall Street Journal reported that Kelce purchased the $5.35 million lakefront estate outside of Cleveland, USA Today reported that the home was acquired in March through an Ohio LLC formed days before the sale. Property tax records list André Eanes, Kelce's longtime business manager, as the recipient of tax correspondence.

articles.title: Kelly Clarkson Claims She Got the “Pretty Woman” Treatment at N.Y.C. Store: ‘You Just Lost a Huge Sale’
articles.summary: “Literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it... Wow, dude. You’re an idiot,” Clarkson said of the Brooklyn store
articles.body:
Kelly Clarkson slammed a Brooklyn store on social media after she said she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford it"

The singer compared the interaction to Julia Roberts' character being dismissed in the 1990 rom-com Pretty Woman

The three-time Grammy winner moved to New York City in 2023 and currently serves as a coach on The Voice season 30

Kelly Clarkson is having a Pretty Woman moment — but not the best kind.

The "Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You)" singer, 44, revealed in a post on X on Saturday, Oct. 10, that she recently went to a New York City store, where she had a less than stellar customer-service experience — similar to the one Julia Roberts ' character Vivian experienced in the 1990 rom-com Pretty Woman .

"Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn't afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me," Clarkson wrote.

"Wow, dude. You're an idiot and just lost a huge sale," she continued, before name dropping the store. She then told her fans to visit the store "if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman , adding, "For sure, check it out 👎."

In her post, she references the Pretty Woman scene in which Vivian goes to a clothing boutique and the salesperson refuses to show her the more expensive items.

In the film, Vivian later returns to the store while wearing nicer clothes and holding tons of shopping bags from other stores as she remarks to the salesperson who refused to show her the items that she made a "Big mistake. Big. Huge."

Clarkson, who moved to New York City in the fall of 2023, doesn't share too many details about her life on social media, often choosing to keep her life private. However, she has shared posts about her experiences and life updates from time to time.

In February, the multi-hyphenate revealed her decision to step back as a daytime host on The Kelly Clarkson Show in an effort to "prioritize" her children — daughter River Rose, 11, and son Remington Alexander, 10 — after the death of their father, Brandon Blackstock .

"There have been so many amazing moments and shows over these seven seasons," she said at the time.

"I am forever grateful and honored to have worked alongside the greatest band and crew you could hope for, all the talent and inspiring people who have shared their time and lives with us, all the fans who have supported our show and to NBC for always being such a supportive and incredible partner," Clarkson added.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

"For now, I want to thank y'all so much for allowing our show to be a part of your lives, and for believing in us and hanging with us for seven incredible years," she concluded in her statement.

The final episode of the show was shot on Aug. 31, nearly seven years after its premiere.

Clarkson is currently starring on the 30th season of The Voice , where she serves as one of the four judges alongside Adam Levine , Queen Latifah and Riley Green .

Comunidade da Área Missionária Nossa Senhora da Conceição Aparecida, em Macapá, celebra o Dia da Padroeira do Brasil. — Foto: Pascom N. Sra. Aparecida/Divulgação

Fiéis da Área Missionária Nossa Senhora da Conceição Aparecida, em Macapá , participam nesta segunda-feira (12) da programação em homenagem à padroeira do Brasil. A agenda inclui oração do Terço, cicloromaria, missa votiva e missa solene, com atividades distribuídas ao longo do dia.

A festividade deste ano tem como tema " Com a Mãe Aparecida, levar a alegria e a esperança a todos os lares" .

A programação do Dia da Padroeira inicia às 6h com a oração do Terço. Logo em seguida, às 6h30, os devotos participam da tradicional Cicloromaria, que deve reunir ciclistas em um momento de fé e homenagem a Nossa Senhora Aparecida.

Ao meio-dia, a comunidade se reúne para a celebração da Missa Votiva. Já às 17h, acontece a Missa Solene, considerada o ponto alto das comemorações, reunindo os fiéis para celebrar a padroeira.

17h - Missa Solene, procissão e Festival Aparecida.

A programação será encerrada no dia 16 de outubro com o tradicional Bingão da Aparecida, a partir das 18h, na área da igreja. O evento contará com mais de R$ 12 mil em prêmios e deve reunir famílias, devotos e membros da comunidade em um momento de confraternização.

articles.title: For over 40 years, Clint Eastwood bought pieces of land to build a 2000-acre land area, most of which is now protected land
articles.summary: Discover Clint Eastwood's journey in creating a 2000-acre sustainable community in Carmel-by-the-Sea, where he has preserved the beauty of nature and protected vital land from development for over 40 years.
articles.body: Clint Eastwood first visited the Carmel-by-the-Sea area in 1951 when he was stationed in the nearby area at Fort Ord as a young Army recruit. He loved the place so much that he started buying pieces of land along the coastal hills and Malpaso Creek in the late 1960s and 1970s, eventually expanding his holdings over several decades into a 2,000+-acre footprint.Clint Eastwood started buying land in the Carmel-by-the-Sea area in the 1960sKnown as Teháma, a private sustainable community located in the hills above Carmel-by-the-Sea and Monterey, California, the actor started investing in land around the 1960s after he fell in love with the coastal area. In 2007, while talking to Land Report about his massive estate and his love for the place, Eastwood shared, “I always liked Carmel. I thought if I could ever afford to or figure out how to make a living there, I might like to live there.”His first investment in the area almost 40 years ago was a “little house as a weekend retreat,” as per the interview, which became the first of many that have now accumulated into a wide 2,000-acre protected community area. Another significant addition to this acreage was the Mission Ranch, which he bought out in 1986. At the time, developers planned to build high-density condominiums on the historic 1850s dairy farm. Eastwood stepped up during his tenure as mayor of Carmel and purchased the 22-acre ranch for roughly USD 5.5 million. He later restored the historic structures and legally protected the surrounding wetlands from future development. The ranch now operates as a thriving hotel and restaurant.Clint Eastwood wanted to protect the land thereThe beloved actor also wished to protect the land that he had fallen in love with in the 1950s. Around 1995, the star sold off approximately 280 coastal acres of land that he owned, which was located near the Malpaso Creek in Monterey County, for USD 3.08 million using California Proposition 70 public conservation funds. The land was then placed under a permanent conservation easement, removing all future residential development rights. To date, the area is part of protected land, and people cannot build or develop anything there.Clint Eastwood established TehámaAccording to the Teháma Carmel Community official website, Eastwood also established the area and turned it into a sustainable community space during his time as the mayor of Carmel. At the time, he connected with Alan Williams and later hired him as a consultant. They came together to create the sustainable community as a way to use up his 2,000 acres of land.Later, in 1997, when he found out about commercial development plans at the mouth of the Carmel River, Eastwood acquired and donated 134 acres of the historic Odello Artichoke Fields, which were valued at approximately USD 6 million, to the Big Sur Land Trust. This ended up forming the core piece of the Carmel River floodplain restoration initiative, another major project that Eastwood supported.85% of the land remains wild and untouched by human developmentThe sustainable community finally came to be in 1999, with over 1,700 acres out of the 2,000 acres permanently set aside for open-space protection, which means that around 85% of the land will remain wild and untouched by commercial development. Not only that, but the development plans are also limited to 90 single-family homesites that are spread across only 300 acres, leaving vast oak woodlands and wildlife spaces intact and untouched.While talking to Land Report about the same, Eastwood had shared, “It’s been amazing how the wild turkeys have done. The deer multiply like crazy. They’ve become much less skittish. Just hanging around for free food. There’s a lot of wildlife there, especially since we put in the golf club. We did it all with native grasses. The only thing we seeded was the greens… We didn’t cut a lot of trees. We moved a few around: 200- and 300-year-old oaks. Slide them 25 yards over. The trees are very healthy up there. Much younger.”As to why he went through all of this effort to preserve the land, Eastwood had explained at the time: “We thought someone might take the land and turn it into a much more congested area or just not take care of it. I thought, someday people are going to want some privacy, and they’ll get tired of living crammed next to each other. And that’s really it.”Clint Eastwood continues to live in a private residential enclave and compound he helped develop in Teháma.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2007, Sandra Bullock bought 91 acres and turned the property into an organic avocado farm
articles.summary: Discover how Sandra Bullock transformed her 91-acre Valley Center property into an organic avocado and citrus farm, blending sustainable living with luxury.
articles.body: Long before her California ranch made headlines in the luxury real estate market, Sandra Bullock had a different plan for the 91-acre property. The Oscar-winning actor wanted to create a place where she could grow her own produce and enjoy a quieter life away from Hollywood. Located in Valley Centre, northeast of San Diego, the estate eventually became an organic avocado and citrus farm, complete with a renovated ranch house and sprawling gardens.Bullock's interest in growing food was not just a feature of the property. In a 2009 interview with Harper's Bazaar, she explained her approach to farming, saying, “If you're going to serve it, you've got to know how to grow it.” She also spoke about wanting to make the ranch organic and self-sustaining. Sandra Bullock bought the 91-acre property in 2007Bullock began acquiring the Valley Center property in 2007 through a trust, according to Mansion Global, which cited property records. The estate covered 91 acres across three parcels and was located about 40 miles northeast of San Diego. Records cited in the report put the purchase price at approximately $2.725 million. The property already had avocado and citrus groves when she bought it. Rather than starting with bare land, Sandra Bullock converted the existing groves to organic production and worked on changing the wider property into a secluded retreat.The estate's main residence was a single-storey adobe ranch house measuring around 5,938 square feet. It featured four bedrooms, six bathrooms, fireplaces and French doors opening onto the gardens. A separate three-bedroom guesthouse gave visitors their own space, while the grounds included a saltwater swimming pool, spa, rose gardens and walking trails. How did the ranch become an organic avocado farm?The agricultural side of the estate was a major part of its appeal. By the time the property was listed for sale in 2022, it had around 1,200 organic avocado trees, alongside citrus and other trees. The grounds also featured imported olive trees, eucalyptus, landscaped gardens and a pond.Bullock's plans went beyond growing fruit. In her 2009 interview with Harper's Bazaar, she described wanting the ranch to be organic and self-sustaining, while acknowledging that organic farming was difficult and expensive. Her comments offered a glimpse of the practical work behind the property, rather than presenting it simply as a celebrity escape.The estate also included solar features and electric-vehicle charging stations, blending its rural setting with modern conveniences. Its combination of agricultural land, gardens and residential space made it both a working farm and a place for family and friends to gather. Sandra Bullock has long enjoyed restoring propertiesReal estate has been a long-standing interest for Bullock. During a 2021 appearance on the SmartLess podcast, Sandra Bullock spoke about her interest in restoring properties and discovering their history.“If I weren't an actress, I'd be a restorer,” she said, describing the satisfaction she found in bringing a property back to life. That interest helps explain the attention she gave to the Valley Center estate. The ranch was not only about acreage or a large house; it brought together restoration, gardening and the opportunity to create a more private setting.The California ranch sold for $5.6 millionSandra Bullock listed the property for $6 million in September 2022. It went under contract within about three weeks and sold for $5.6 million, with the sale closing in early November that year, according to Mansion Global.The sale brought an end to her ownership of the ranch after roughly 15 years. Its appeal lay in the mix of open land, established organic groves, guest accommodation and a renovated home surrounded by gardens.For Bullock, the Valley Center property reflected an interest she had spoken about herself: growing food and restoring places with character. What began as a 91-acre purchase became a private California retreat shaped by her vision for an organic, self-sustaining ranch.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Saba Ali Pataudi opens up on inheriting Tiger Pataudi's Rs 1000 crore legacy of Bhopal Trust and lessons from the former captain of Indian cricket team: 'I imbibed qualities of being fair,  not losing my cool from him'
articles.summary: Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi popularly called Tiger Pataudi is still remembered as one India's most celebrated cricketers and the former captain of the Indian
articles.body: Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi popularly called Tiger Pataudi is still remembered as one India's most celebrated cricketers and the former captain of the Indian cricket team. He married Sharmila Tagore and had three children, Saba Ali Pataudi, Saif Ali Khan and Soha Ali Khan. In a recent interview, Saba has opened up on her legacy and the teachings from her father. She also spoke about her responsibilities in Bhopal and the trust associated with her family's heritage.Talking about her bond with her father, Saba described him as someone she continues to turn to spiritually, even after his passing. She recalled how he guided her in understanding her responsibilities and taught her the importance of fairness, composure and choosing her words carefully.“He was my 'go-to'. Spiritually, I talk to him in my own way. He was my everything. He taught me what I needed to know, in terms of Bhopal and the work I do. He left me that legacy to take forward. My mother told me that take the best from both of us. In an interview she said, 'Saif is like me and Soha is like Tiger but Saba has a bit of both of us'. But with him, I imbibed qualities of being fair, being just, being proper. He said that don't lose your cool. You're only losing your own temper, it doesn't make any sense. Keeping your cool and being precise, I can verbalise what I need to say but I won't shout and scream. I don't need to. Being careful with words, I learnt from him.”When asked whether the legacy she had inherited from her father was worth over Rs 1,000 crore, Saba spoke about the family's responsibilities in Bhopal and its association with the Rubaths in Makkah and Medina. The Rubaths are facilities associated with providing accommodation and support to pilgrims travelling for Hajj.“Yes, the Bhopal it's in fact is responsible for Makkah and Medina as well. The Rubaths, which means that when the hajis go for hajj from Bhopal and taking care of their stay and so we acquire buildings and we have to kind of, in Bhopal itself I'm also responsible for only the monuments that come under the Aukaf-e-Shahi which is the trust fund that my father and grandmother had.”She further explained that her responsibilities include overseeing the upkeep of mosques and other buildings that fall under the Aukaf-e-Shahi trust, along with managing the logistical aspects associated with their maintenance.She added, “So the mosques and any buildings under their trust is what I take care of in the upkeep and you know things like logistically in that regard. It does involve a lot of money but money that does not come back to India or does not get personally used at all to clarify. It's a charity organisation which is run by Saudi, independently but we are affiliated and so it's a very, mashallah I would say, a prestigious position to be in which is a legacy that of course he thought I was more equipped and had the time and also very Islamic in my way that he thought would suit me to take it forward and take care of.”Tiger Pataudi passed away on September 22, 2011, at the age of 70, following a lung infection.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Spalletti: ‘Kolo Muani needs to put his best skills into practice’
articles.summary: Luciano Spalletti says he hopes that Juventus have learned from their mistakes away against Cagliari last season ahead of their meeting in Serie A on Sunday...
articles.body:
Luciano Spalletti says he hopes that Juventus have learned from their mistakes away against Cagliari last season ahead of their meeting in Serie A on Sunday evening, and has told Randal Kolo Muani to 'stay calm' and put his best skills into practice.

Juventus come into tonight's game two points behind Cagliari in the Serie A table after five matches, but a victory this evening will see them leapfrog their opponents into third place in the standings.

Spalletti previews Cagliari vs. Juventus

REGGIO NELL'EMILIA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Luciano Spalletti Head Coach of Juventus looks on prior to the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and Juventus at Mapei Stadium – Citta' del Tricolore on September 13, 2026 in Reggio nell'Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

Juventus were beaten 1-0 by Cagliari in this fixture last season, back in January earlier this year. Speaking to DAZN ahead of kick-off, Spalletti said that he hopes to avoid the same outcome this time around.

"We encountered some difficulties after that defeat and we want to be ready so that it doesn't happen again. This is a game we have to take by the hands. Cagliari is a tricky customer and they play good football."

Spalletti was also asked for his thoughts on centre-forward Kolo Muani, who has gone five games without a goal in Serie A since making his return to the club over the summer transfer window.

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus reacts during the Serie A match between Juventus and Atalanta BC at Allianz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

The Bianconeri head coach warns that he will not get the best out of himself during matches if he does not play to his own strengths.

"There is a risk that he is too markable," said Spalletti. "He's not the player who holds off his man and draws in opposition defenders. He likes to dribble, come in with speed, those are his best qualities. He has to stay calm and put them into practice."

Spalletti also had praise for Nico Gonzalez, who has been in impressive form since returning from a loan spell with Atletico Madrid over the summer.

"Nico has a wickedness about him and that desire to bring home whatever he wants in football. He determines everything that happens to him."

articles.title: Kourtney Kardashian's expletive-filled reaction to Oscar-winning actress calling her 'annoying'

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney doubles down with topless sports betting ad weeks after backlash:  ‘I’m flattered’
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney's new Novig ad shows the "Euphoria" star ditching her top and covering herself with footballs amid fierce women in sports backlash.
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney is doubling down on her controversial Novig sports betting ads. On Sunday, the "Euphoria" star ditched her top in a new commercial for the prediction market platform, wearing only white Novig underwear while strategically covering herself with footballs. "There are grown men making spreadsheets to bet on what color underwear I’m wearing," Sweeney says in the ad posted on Instagram. "I mean, I’m flattered?" SYDNEY SWEENEY’S PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD 'REINFORCES THE IMAGE SHE HAS ALREADY BUILT' DESPITE BACKLASH: EXPERT She then jokes about someone "betting their 401(k) on a war" before concluding, "Novig is … just sports." The new campaign comes weeks after Sweeney’s first Novig advertisement sparked fierce backlash from female athletes and critics who accused the company of sexualizing women in sports. EXCLUSIVE: STAR FEMALE GOLFER FIRES BACK AT SYDNEY SWEENEY CRITICS: 'SHE'S GOT SEX APPEAL' In the original ad, Sweeney appeared nearly nude while posing with sports equipment and telling viewers the platform was "just sports." The campaign prompted criticism from Olympians and professional athletes, including swimmer Ariarne Titmus, who called it a "kick in the face" to women who have devoted their lives to sports. SHARON STONE TELLS SYDNEY SWEENEY TO 'TAKE RESPONSIBILITY' FOR PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD Gymnast Gracie Kramer accused the ad of marketing women’s sports "through the male gaze," while British sprinter Amy Hunt said the campaign offered an inaccurate picture of what women in sports look like. Adrienne Uthe, founder of Kronus Communications, previously told Fox News Digital that while Sweeney's ad may have ruffled feathers, "women having agency also means allowing women to make choices about their image that other women may not personally agree with." "People are entitled to dislike the ad, just like women athletes are entitled to criticize it for their own reasons," Uthe said. "But I don't think this is materially damaging to Sydney Sweeney in any way, shape or form. "In fact, I don't think it's a large departure from who she is and what her brand represents. She's a beautiful woman right now at the peak of her career, and she ultimately can decide which projects she wants to take and which ones she doesn't." BROADCAST BIAS: MEDIA BASH SYDNEY SWEENEY, BUT COVER FOR LEFTIST MACKLEMORE She added, "And she's chosen to make sexuality a part of her brand for better or for worse." Novig defended the original advertisement as a "fun idea" created with "confidence, humor and a playful edge." The latest campaign is not the first time Sweeney has found herself at the center of a major advertising controversy. In 2025, her American Eagle campaign, titled "Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans," drew backlash over a promotional video that played on the words "genes" and "jeans." articles.title: Aaron Sorkin’s ‘Social Reckoning’ is off to a weak start
articles.summary: What does this mean for a fall full of movies starring villainous tech CEOs?
articles.body:
“The Social Reckoning,” Aaron Sorkin’s follow-up to “The Social Network,” is on-track to make only $5.5 million at the domestic box office this weekend, according to Sunday estimates.

That’s below the already underwhelming $7 million to $8 million the studio had projected, and it means Sorkin’s new movie is unlikely to become a “Social Network”-sized hit. The earlier film had a $22 million opening weekend and made a total of $97 million domestically (and that’s at 2010 ticket prices). It also won Sorkin an Oscar and became one of most influential on-screen depictions of Silicon Valley and startup culture.

Beyond the fate of a single film, the weekend box office could also offer hints about audience excitement, or lack thereof, as we kick off a fall full of movies starring villainous, real-world tech CEOs . There’s Alex Gibney’s four-hour documentary “Musk” (which also opened this weekend), Nathan Fielder’s apparently uncategorizable Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” (coming next weekend!), and the OpenAI boardroom drama “Artificial” (which has a new distributor after being dropped by Amazon).

Outside of theaters, Netflix also has a series called “The Altruists” coming in November , telling the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the collapse of FTX.

As for “The Social Reckoning,” while “The Social Network” was a notable success, the theatrical landscape has changed significantly in the last 16 years. And where the first film focused on the excitement and drama of Facebook’s early days, the sequel is darker and heavier — it’s all about whistleblower Frances Haugen’s decision to leak what became known as the Facebook files.

So maybe a movie about Senate hearings and algorithm changes was never going to be a big hit. Or maybe “The Social Reckoning”’s real audience is among older moviegoers who have only returned sporadically to theaters . And I wonder if critiquing Facebook feels a bit less urgent to audiences who are more likely to be losing sleep over AI.

Maybe just as importantly, the new movie’s reviews just aren’t very good . (For what it’s worth, I enjoyed “The Social Reckoning” but will fully admit that it’s overloaded Sorkin’s trademark speechifying. And I couldn’t help dreaming about a version directed — like the original — by David Fincher, with a score by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross.)

“Musk,” meanwhile, made $69,000 during its opening weekend in four theaters. It will roll out more broadly in the coming weeks, but given its length and subject matter, the documentary will probably reach many more viewers once it starts streaming on HBO Max.

articles.title: Ben Affleck says political 'hypocrisy, corruption and failure' left him 'disillusioned'
articles.summary: Ben Affleck calls U.S. politics "terrible" and "tawdry" while promoting "Animals," a new movie in which he plays an L.A. mayoral candidate.
articles.body: Ben Affleck has no interest in running for public office. The "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" star told Variety that trying to become a politician sounds "terrible" and "tawdry" to him. "I just think that’s enormously — I don’t know, man, that seems terrible," Affleck told the outlet while promoting a new movie in which he plays a candidate for L.A. mayor. "There’s a reason why political stories are often chosen as parables for moral compromise. You really get thrust up into the contrast between the ideal version of us and how we should be in our lives and the way it is." BEN AFFLECK DIRECTS, STARS IN NETFLIX KIDNAPPING THRILLER 'ANIMALS' COMING THIS OCTOBER The 54-year-old called politics a "very depressing world, in my opinion. Tawdry. And that has no appeal to me." He also declined to tell the outlet who he was backing for mayor in Los Angeles this November. "I haven’t thought about being asked that. I don’t know if, given this movie, my endorsement harms or helps anybody," he admitted. "I should stay agnostic, at least until the movie comes out." Affleck told Good Morning America on Wednesday that he believes the "collective bar for politics because of the way the political world has sort of evolved has gotten so low that there’s this kind of like, you know, people are just sort of looking for like just ‘Somebody shoot me straight.’’" FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS WANT MAJOR CHANGE AMID ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL DISCONTENT He added that there’s a sense in the country, whether you’re a Democrat or a Republican that "we’re not doing a very good job. We have a system that’s kind of failing us." Playing a man running for mayor taught him: "This is not all that much fun. And it would be a hard way — you’re just raising money all the time." NETFLIX DROPS FULL TRAILER FOR BEN AFFLECK'S 'ANIMALS' AND EXPECTATIONS ARE ALREADY SOARING He said that he and the man playing his campaign manager in the movie decided one day to take campaign shirts and hats with the name of his character, go out in L.A. and claim he was running for mayor. When he told people he was running as his character, Affleck said voters would ask for a selfie, they seemed interested and "people would launch into their whole thing and I was like ‘If I’m not careful, I’m going to win this.'" MICHAEL RAPAPORT DOUBLES DOWN ON 2029 NYC MAYORAL RUN, VOWS 'STREET FIGHT' AGAINST ZOHRAN MAMDANI "Do not vote for me for mayor!" he joked to the camera. Affleck explained that his movie "Animals" is about the moral compromises people make. "The extremely effective nature of when a person individually has something to lose is when they're most apt to make compromises," he says. "Are we just kind of self-seeking animals who, in retrospect, build stories to rationalize where we are and what we've done? articles.title: Vinicius y Virginia vuelven a separarse
articles.summary: Cuatro meses después de reconciliarse
articles.body: VinIcius y Virginia Fonseca han terminado su relación cuatro meses después de reconciliarse, según publicaron este domingo medios brasileños. Portavoces de Virginia informaron a medios locales que "no hubo pelea ni conflicto" y que simplemente decidieron no seguir juntos. Ni el futbolista ni la influencer, quien se encuentra de viaje con sus hijos en Miami, se han pronunciado públicamente sobre el asunto. Sin embargo, el sábado Virginia publicó en redes un texto motivacional en el que expresaba su intención de "apartarse" de lo que le hacía "daño", así como de las "energías negativas" y la "falta de reciprocidad". La relación entre los dos empezó el año pasado y tuvo un primer parón en mayo, poco antes del Mundial de Estados Unidos. Después del torneo, se les vio pasando las vacaciones juntos en un yate en el Mediterráneo, una confirmación de que habían retomado el noviazgo. Hace poco más de un mes intercambiaron anillos de compromiso y se dejaron ver por el GP de España que se celebró en Madrid.

articles.title: Kelly Clarkson says a Brooklyn store snubbed her. The shop says the item she wanted wasn’t for sale.
articles.summary: Clarkson blasted Art of Play, alleging it treated her like she “couldn’t afford” its merchandise. The store says the resulting backlash was “surreal.”
articles.body: Kelly Clarkson accused a New York City store of treating her as though she couldn’t afford its merchandise. But the business at the center of her viral complaint offered a different explanation. Clarkson, a three-time Grammy winner, publicly called out Art of Play in Brooklyn, writing Saturday on X that she visited the curiosity shop with “a few things in mind to buy” and was offered something similar after being treated as though she couldn’t afford what she wanted. “Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” Clarkson wrote of the employee who served her at the store. She compared the experience to the scene in “Pretty Woman” in which Julia Roberts’ character is snubbed at an upscale boutique, urging people to visit the store “if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character.” Clarkson’s accusation sparked swift backlash against Art of Play, leading many social media users to criticize it and leave negative online reviews. Art of Play said Sunday in a statement on Instagram that Clarkson asked about purchasing Molly, a “one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton.” The mechanical bird wasn’t for sale, the store said, because it “plays an important role in the magic shows we host here.” “However, the negative experience Kelly described on twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop,” the store wrote. It added that all visitors to Art of Play are “equally welcome.” The statement, which offered an explanation for why Clarkson couldn’t buy the bird, didn’t directly address her allegation that an employee had treated her as though she “couldn’t afford” its merchandise. Art of Play described the reaction to Clarkson’s post as overwhelming. “Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store,” it added. “It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity.” Art of Play’s response Sunday fueled further debate online over whether Clarkson misinterpreted the interaction and whether her decision to publicly name the small business was warranted. Representatives for Clarkson and Art of Play didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. Clarkson is a coach on NBC’s “The Voice” and the former host of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” which also aired on the network. NBC is a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News. The incident has ignited some discourse about whether bias plays into stores’ treatment of customers. Some online speculated that Clarkson may have taken offense because she wasn’t recognized, while others argued that she was asking to be treated decently as a customer regardless of whether the business knew of her wealth and status. In its statement, Art of Play thanked its community for its support and welcomed “all the curious folks who have discovered us amidst the drama.” The store also referred to one of Clarkson’s most famous lyrics. “We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday,” Art of Play wrote. “As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.’”

articles.title: Tobey Maguire officiates his ex-wife’s wedding just weeks after finalizing divorce
articles.summary: The couple separated in 2016, but took a decade to formally dissolve their marriage.
articles.body:
Tobey Maguire officiated his ex-wife Jennifer Meyer's wedding to Geoffrey Ogunlesi.

The marriage comes just weeks after Maguire and Meyer finalized their divorce.

The former couple, who share two kids, separated in 2016.

Jennifer Meyer has officially tied the knot with Geoffrey Ogunlesi — and her ex-husband Tobey Maguire played a key role in the ceremony.

According to photos of the wedding obtained by PEOPLE , the Spider-Man actor officiated his ex-wife's wedding to Ogunlesi, the son of Nigerian billionaire lawyer and investment banker Adebayo Ogunlesi. The couple said "I do" on Saturday, just weeks after Meyer and Maguire finalized their divorce.

Meyer and Ogunlesi wed at the Four Seasons Resort Lanai in Hawaii. The ceremony was attended by a star-studded roster of guests, including Rachel Zoe, Courteney Cox, Kate Hudson, Leonardo DiCaprio and girlfriend Vittoria Ceretti, along with Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos.

Also in attendance were Meyer and Maguire's two children — daughter Ruby, 19, and son Otis, 17 — along with the newborn baby girl whom Meyer and Ogunlesi welcomed in May.

Maguire and Meyer, a jewelry designer, met in 2003 while he was shooting Seabiscuit . They tied the knot in a Hawaii wedding ceremony in September 2007 before ultimately separating in June 2016, just three months shy of their ninth anniversary.

The decision came about "after much soul searching and consideration," said the parents of two at the time, adding, "Our first priority remains raising our children together with enduring love, respect, and friendship."

Four years later, Meyer petitioned for divorce. It would be another five years before Maguire filed his own response in July 2025. The divorce was finalized on Sept. 21, more than 10 years after their split.

By that point, Meyer was engaged to Ogunlesi and the couple had just welcomed their first baby together. After the birth of her daughter, Meyer told PEOPLE she had built a close-knit blended family with Maguire, their kids, and Ogunlesi.

"When Tobey and I broke up, it was very clear immediately that Ruby and Otis came first, and we really cared about each other as people, and we wanted to be in each other's lives no matter what," she shared. "And we didn't want to miss a Christmas. We didn't want to miss a Thanksgiving."

She continued, "We travel all together. We have every holiday together. We have every birthday all together. He is an incredible father. He is an incredible ex-husband. And Geoff loves him and he loves Geoff. And so everything just works."

In the years since her split from the Babylon actor, Meyer has emphasized that the former couple remain close and are coparenting harmoniously, despite a few bumps in the road.

"It was a choice, and it was trusting in, like, the universe has got our back," she said of coparenting during a 2022 appearance on World's First Podcast . "But let me tell you something, the work is a motherf-----."

She shared that what keeps them on track is making sure their children remain their "first priority."

As for her enduring friendship with Maguire, she added, "I can't even explain [it]. He is my brother. I love him to death."

articles.title: Russell Brand is on trial for rape and sexual assault. His career has been a catalog of controversy
articles.summary: A look at the career of comedian and actor Russell Brand, who will stand trial in London on Monday, accused of rape and sexual assault.
articles.body:
British comedian and actor Russell Brand will stand trial in London on Monday, accused of rape and sexual assault .

The 51-year-old has pleaded not guilty to three charges of rape, one charge of indecent assault and three counts of sexual assault, relating to six women.

The charges go back to the beginning of his career.

Brand became a household name in British television in the early 2000s, presenting the talk show "Celebrity Big Brother's Big Mouth," a spin-off from the popular reality series "Celebrity Big Brother," and receiving accolades such as Best Male Comedy Newcomer at the British Comedy Awards for his talk show "Russell Brand's Got Issues."

As well as garnering many TV fans, his eccentric stand-up performances made him one of the UK's most popular live entertainers.

Brand's energetic character and provocative jokes, often relating to sex, made him a distinctive voice in the UK media. In 2006, he became host of "The Russell Brand Show" on BBC Radio 2, a weekly Saturday night program during which he had frank, comedic — and often X-rated — conversations with a co-host and guests.

While the popular radio show attracted around 400,000 listeners on average, it came to an abrupt halt in 2008 when Brand quit the show after offensive voice messages, left by him and entertainer Jonathan Ross for "Fawlty Towers" star Andrew Sachs, were aired on the program, sparking outrage and breaching UK broadcasting regulations.

In the voice messages, Brand joked — using explicit language — about having sex with Sachs' granddaughter. He and Ross went on to say that Sachs, who was 78 at the time, might kill himself on hearing the news. The episode was widely criticized, with the BBC receiving tens of thousands of complaints and regulator Ofcom receiving almost 2,000.

Even the British prime minister of the day, Gordon Brown, reacted to what was later labeled "Sachsgate," calling Brand's comments "inappropriate and unacceptable."

At the time, Brand said he took "complete responsibility," adding: "I got a bit caught up in the moment and forgot that, at the core of the rude comments and silly songs, were the real feelings of a beloved and brilliant comic actor and a very sweet and big-hearted young woman."

However, he changed his tone five years later in a BBC Radio interview. While he admitted that listeners' offense was "genuine" and apologized for his "wrong" actions, he also said that "there was obviously a pre-existing agenda in privately owned media to destabilize, attack and diminish the BBC."

Despite the notoriety of Sachsgate, Brand's rise was only briefly impeded.

The same year he quit his radio show, his Channel 4 TV show "Russell Brand's Ponderland" was nominated for a BAFTA, and he became a recognized name in Hollywood after portraying the hedonistic rock star Aldous Snow in the romantic comedy "Forgetting Sarah Marshall." Two years later, he reprised the role in the spinoff "Get Him to the Greek."

It was around this time that he began dating US pop star Katy Perry . The high-profile relationship didn't last, however. After marrying in October 2010 , the couple were fending off divorce rumors by 2011 and, by the end of that year , Brand had announced he was divorcing Perry , reportedly catching the singer off guard.

Perry revealed in 2013 that Brand told her that he was divorcing her via a text on New Year's Eve and that she hadn't heard from him since, adding that while he "wanted an equal" at first, strong men "get that equal and they're like, I can't handle the equalness. He didn't like the atmosphere of me being the boss on tour. So that was really hurtful, and it was very controlling, which was upsetting."

Brand, however, blamed busy schedules for their split , and said in 2017 that the up-and-down nature of fame contributed to the brevity of the marriage. He said he still felt "very warm towards her."

Brand has credited yoga and meditation for helping him deal with addictions to drugs, alcohol and sex.

In 2017, he wrote a self-help guide, "Recovery: Freedom From Our Addictions."

He had previously published his autobiography, "My Booky Wook: A Memoir of Sex, Drugs, and Stand-Up," which became a best-seller in the UK and was published in the US two years later. Critics described the book as "funny and frequently awful, " as well as a "relentless ride with a comic mind clearly at the wheel."

Brand's stand-up shows and podcasts began to focus more on societal trends, spirituality, psychology and childbirth, and his on-stage performances moved from theater stages to speaking at wellness gatherings, such as Wanderlust Wellspring in Palm Springs, California in 2018.

With his second wife — author Laura Gallacher, whom he married in 2017 and with whom he has three children — Brand launched a spirituality festival in Wales, titled "Community," which had its first outing in 2023. A subsequent edition was postponed and then canceled.

More recently, Brand has been hosting a podcast, "Stay Free," and making YouTube videos for his "Awakened Wonders" online community – paying members with whom he shares his thoughts on spirituality, culture, politics and global affairs.

Brand promotes his community as a counter to what he describes as the "corrupted and broken" old systems that govern the world, with "a New Spirit" being born among them.

He frequently airs conspiracy theories about a "concealed agenda" and deception by governments, Big Pharma and Big Tech, as well as voicing suspicions about the Covid vaccine, and corruption and dishonesty in the mainstream media.

In a YouTube video published in September 2023, Brand accused the British government of trying to censor him online, and he has described the claims against him as "coordinated" and "egregious attacks" by the media, questioning, "Is there another agenda at play?"

articles.title: Robert Pattinson on new film Primetime and how hunting predators became hit TV
articles.summary: The actor portrays the real-life host of American TV show, To Catch a Predator, in his latest film.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson is having quite the year.

The British actor has already starred opposite Zendaya in The Drama, and played a key role in summer blockbuster The Odyssey.

But his new film, Primetime, takes him in a completely new direction - as he portrays the real-life host of American TV show, To Catch a Predator.

The show, which aired from 2004 to 2007, involved hunting alleged child abusers.

For Pattinson, who became a father almost three years ago, the film's plot is particularly concerning.

"It's both the most terrifying thing that can happen to you, whether you're a parent, or even if you're not," he told BBC News at the film's screening at London Film Festival.

"It's the most unimaginable sin possible," he added.

The new A24 crime thriller depicts the show's host, NBC journalist Chris Hansen, carrying out sting operations on would-be predators.

But it also led to questions over where to draw the line between investigative journalism, police activity and reality television.

Speaking on Sunday night, Pattinson reflected on the show's complicated legacy.

"The show was this kind of microcosm of saying, 'oh, we can do something about [child abuse], and we can do something about it really, really, really quickly," he said.

"And in some ways, that's correct, but it also makes for incredibly powerful TV, and that's when it gets into slightly dicey territory."

When asked whether he thinks attitudes towards entertainment have now changed, Pattinson paused.

"I think on mainstream TV, but then it's just been replaced," he replied, pointing out that similar content has since appeared on social media.

"That's why I was interested in the show, because I could see the beginning of a new wave of 'predator catching' in pretty much the same format that it was in the early 2000s," he said. "And I was just interested as to why that was happening."

"And it got bigger and bigger and bigger, and now it's one of the most massive things on social media."

Hansen himself has been critical of the film, calling it "bizarre" and "detached from reality" in a video posted on X .

Addressing his criticisms, director Lance Oppenheim said: "I agree, that was by design.

"I always thought of this movie as more of a fever dream than something that was representational portrait."

Oppenheim added there was something "ancient" about the desire to watch people getting publicly punished.

"It's happened for thousands of years," he added. "I wanted to make something that interrogated that."

Oppenheim, who is also currently co-directing with Nathan Fielder a highly anticipated documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, said separately of that project: "I want everyone to see it. It's a really special movie."

Pattinson, 40, became something of a pin-up after playing vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight series, alongside American actress Kristen Stewart.

Before that, he stole young hearts as Hufflepuff hunk Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.

He has since starred in major films including Christopher Nolan's Tenet, as well as a range of eccentric, indie films.

This year, he has been on a roll, with Dune: Part Three still to come.

He’s also got the next Batman film in the pipeline, although production on that has reportedly paused . When asked when they'll be back to work, Pattinson didn’t give much away ("We don't know yet, but yeah, working on it.")

Primetime has also led to speculation that this could be the year that Pattinson gets his first ever Oscars nomination. Is that likely, I wonder?

"I am eternally grateful that I got these jobs," he responds.

"But then [to have] been able to even do them, this is one of the best years of my life."

articles.title: Ella Langley says canceled concert was ‘not worth a human life’ after bomb threat
articles.summary: Ella Langley became emotional during her Texas concert explaining why she canceled her sold-out BOK Center show despite Tulsa police finding no credible threat.
articles.body: Ella Langley is speaking out about her decision to cancel her concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma, following a reported bomb threat. The 27-year-old country star addressed the cancellation while performing in Lubbock, Texas, one day after calling off her sold-out Friday night show at Tulsa's BOK Center. Langley became emotional while explaining why she decided not to perform despite police finding no credible threat. MEGAN MORONEY CANCELS SHOW MID-PERFORMANCE, LEAVES STAGE IN TEARS "I was put in charge of a decision for 15,000 people and I decided to make the decision that I could live with the rest of my life," the "Choosin' Texas" hitmaker told the crowd on Saturday night at the United Supermarkets Arena, according to Taste of Country. "Because when it comes to keeping you safe and making sure that this show is a safe place for us to come and enjoy our music, then it will happen," she continued. "But the second, it feels like it's not, I'm not doing it. I'm not doing it because a concert's not worth a human life. It's not." ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT "And so I would have made yesterday's decision ten billion times over," she added. "And I'd do it tomorrow and I'd do it the next day." Langley went on to explain that the safety of her fans outweighed her desire to perform. "Because while I'm grateful to get to do what I do, it's not the most important thing in this life," she said. "What's the most important thing in this life is the people around you that love you and that are there for you no matter what." "The most important thing in this life is that you wake up every day and feel like, 'You know what, I'm good today. I am so grateful to have woken up today,'" Langley continued. ELLA LANGLEY DELIVERS POWERFUL FAITH MESSAGE TO CROWD DURING MORGAN WALLEN CONCERT IN CHICAGO "The most important thing in this life, number one, is your relationship with Jesus Christ," she added. Langley admitted that she nearly canceled Saturday's concert in Texas because she was still shaken by the incident. However, she credited her faith in Jesus with giving her the courage to return to the stage. ELLA LANGLEY GOES VIRAL WITH PASSIONATE COMMENTS ABOUT HER CHRISTIAN FAITH, GOD, LOVE AND RELIGION "If it wasn't for Him," I would have canceled this show tonight," she told the crowd. "I would have." "But I felt this calling and this tug in my chest saying, 'It's OK. We are safe. We can do this show,'" Langley continued. "And I decided to do it because of Him right there. And that's the only reason." ELLA LANGLEY'S FAITH AND AUTHENTICITY FUEL RECORD-BREAKING RISE, EXPERTS SAY "I'm not gonna live in fear," Langley added. "We're going to put on music and get to do this for the rest of our lives. And I know that. I know because this is my calling. This is the thing that I was called to do, and I'm going to continue doing it. Nobody is going to take me out of it or scare me out." Langley expressed her gratitude to her fans for coming to her Texas show despite the frightening incident at the Oklahoma concert. "I know yesterday was scary, it was scary for all of us," she said. "But we're just so grateful to be playing this show tonight. We're so grateful and we will never take this for granted. We love it, we love what we do. I wouldn't trade it for the world." "Tonight I can tell that y'all knew that I've needed what you've given me. And this band and this crew — you knew that we needed this show tonight, so thank you so much for giving it to us," Langley added. ED SHEERAN'S GILLETTE STADIUM CONCERTS CALLED OFF AS TROUBLED TOUR FACES FRESH SETBACK Langley announced the cancelation of Friday night's concert on Instagram approximately two hours before the show was scheduled to begin. "Due to a serious security threat involving the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team, the incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show. This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team," the singer began. She said the decision followed guidance from local authorities, venue officials and her security team, adding that she refused to put anyone in danger. "I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am. This is not a decision that was made lightly. I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way," the country music star's statement concluded. The BOK Center also released a statement on Friday. "The safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed. We understand the disappointment this news brings and apologize to fans who planned to attend. The safety of fans is our foremost concern and will always come first," the statement read. The official Instagram account for the BOK Center said that ticket refunds and additional information will be shared as soon as possible. Langley's explanation for her decision to cancel the concert comes after the Tulsa Police Department said that they found no credible threat to the event. In a since-deleted statement posted to Facebook, the department explained that officers had conducted routine security sweeps before the concert using K-9 units, bomb technicians, patrol officers and venue security personnel and "did not find anything" dangerous. "A call was made threatening the lives of people attending the event," they continued. "Out of an abundance of caution, we swept the building and surrounding area and again found no credible threat to the event's safety. We advised the performer's staff that we found no credible threat to the event, but they decided to cancel the performance anyway." Richard Meulenberg provided additional details in a video posted to Facebook that has since been deleted. Meulenberg said that after the first security sweeps, "the event was ready to go," according to Saving Country Music. "And then what happened was a call came in, saying that someone was going to [do] great harm to the people here at this event in the way of shots fired and bombs. So we came out again in an overabundance of caution, used our bomb dogs again, searched the entire area, we could not find a credible threat here at the BOK Center," he said. "We apologize to everyone who came down to the Tulsa area for this. But everything is safe." In an interview with Tulsa news station Fox23, Meulenberg also emphasized that the department did not recommend canceling the concert. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? We advised the group here that was supposed to perform that we could not find a credible threat. We never advised them they should not continue to have their event. articles.title: Kelly Clarkson Calls Brooklyn Store Owner ‘Rude’ and a ‘Liar’ in Fiery Response to Their Claims About Her “Pretty Woman” Experience
articles.summary: “So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it,” Clarkson wrote of the Brooklyn business’ claims
articles.body:
Kelly Clarkson is responding to a New York City shop owner who disputed her claims about being told she couldn't buy a $15,000 item

Art of Play said the singing bird automaton Clarkson asked about is permanently attached to the wall

Clarkson shared a photo she said showed the item's $15,000 price tag displayed beside it

Kelly Clarkson is firing back at a New York City shop owner who disputed her claims about being denied a sale for a $15,000 item .

On Sunday, Oct. 11, the singer, 44, responded to the claims made by the Brooklyn store Art of Play , which said that the item she was trying to purchase is "permanently attached to the wall and isn't for sale," despite Clarkson claiming it had a price tag on display.

"Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn't for sale," she shared in a sarcastic Instagram Stories post. "That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with — so the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn't happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone, 'Yes, it's for sale but it costs $15,000, so if you'd like me to find something comparable for you I can.' That all never happened and now it's not for sale."

On Saturday, Oct. 10, the "Stronger (What Doesn't Kill You)" artist said that, after driving to Brooklyn to check out the shop, she was met with an experience similar to the one that Julia Roberts ' character, Vivian, experienced in the 1990 rom-com Pretty Woman.

"Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn't afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me," she wrote on X . "Wow, dude. You're an idiot and just lost a huge sale."

One day after Clarkson shared her experience, the store — which is home to a "unique collection of home goods, puzzles, games, toys and books," according to its website — addressed the singer's claims, writing on social media that she "inquired about buying 'Molly,' a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here."

"Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn't for sale," Art of Play wrote on Instagram .

Emphasizing that the "negative experience" Clarkson described would surely "resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop," the business stated that it welcomes everyone.

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store," the business continued. "It's been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity."

Clarkson — who moved to New York City in the fall of 2023 — also shared a grainy photo in another Instagram Stories post that apparently showed the item hanging on the wall with a price tag next to it.

"So you're not only rude, you're also a liar. Got it," the mom of two wrote. "And by the way, I obviously support small businesses because I was literally at a small business trying to purchase things. I love small businesses and know they are important and I always support them, but you don't get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business."

"It's not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool," Clarkson added. "Unfortunately, you aren't."

articles.title: Netanyahu demands probe into sources for award-winning Gaza film NAZA
articles.summary: Documentary draws on 24 anonymous Israeli sources accusing military of killing Palestinians in Gaza using AI systems.
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has called for an investigation into the anonymous sources featured in a documentary alleging that Israel’s military killed civilians in Gaza using AI-powered targeting systems.

The award-winning film, NAZA, draws on testimony from 24 unnamed Israeli military whistleblowers accusing the army of using the systems to kill numerous civilians in the besieged territory.

“I demand that the chief of general staff, the head of the Shin Bet, and the attorney general launch a comprehensive investigation into the participants in the film ‘Naza’ and prosecute them for serious information security violations, criminal libel, and harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests,” Netanyahu said on X on Saturday evening.

“The film presents a false, misleading, and biased narrative that defames the State of Israel and the [Israeli military] internationally, severely damaging Israel’s standing,” he added.

In a statement last month, the Israeli military said it “categorically” rejected the whistleblowers’ allegations, calling some of their assertions “absurd’ and contradictory.

It insisted that the selection and approval of strikes “are made by human personnel only”, in line with the military’s guidelines.

Israeli army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has called for legal action against the participants to be considered and ordered an investigation into suspected leaks of classified military information used in the film’s production.

NAZA takes its name from the Israeli military term for civilian casualties expected in air strikes, an abbreviated form of the Hebrew phrase for “collateral damage”.

The film was awarded a special jury prize at the Venice International Film Festival and received a historic 25-minute standing ovation.

It has also triggered a political storm in Israel.

The film’s directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, have been accused of “treason”. Netanyahu and Culture Minister Miki Zohar have threatened to revoke their Israeli citizenship.

Last week, the head of Israel’s National Public Diplomacy Directorate, Tzipi Hotovely, awarded the creators of another film, NAZA: The Real Story, certificates of recognition for countering the “blood libels” made in the original NAZA film.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office, NAZA: The Real Story features testimony from soldiers refuting the original claims.

In contrast, 43 Israeli rights groups defended the filmmakers of NAZA and denounced the threats being directed at them, according to Israel’s Channel 12 news.

Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began on October 7, 2023, after Hamas’s armed wing, the Qassam Brigades, and other Palestinian groups attacked southern Israel, killing 1,139 people and taking about 240 captive.

Since then, Israel has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,000 children, according to Gaza’s Ministry of Health.

articles.title: ‘I couldn’t even brush my teeth’: Mirnaa Menon recalls health scare during Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' shoot; actress took injection and tablets before shoot
articles.summary: Actor Mirnaa Menon has opened up about a difficult day on the sets of 'Jailer 2'.
articles.body: Actor Mirnaa Menon has opened up about a difficult day on the sets of 'Jailer 2'. She recalled experiencing severe physical discomfort before filming an important scene for the Rajinikanth-starrer. Despite feeling extremely unwell, she decided to reach the location after seeking medical assistance.As reported by Reporter website, Mirnaa Menon said her condition was so bad that she struggled with even basic activities that morning. She initially took tablets brought by her staff, but they did not provide relief. With the shoot scheduled to begin at 6.30 am, she informed her manager that she needed to visit a hospital and would arrive late.“One day, I felt extremely unwell. I couldn't go for the shoot. I had an important scene to shoot that day. I had been feeling very sick since I woke up that morning. So, I called my staff, and they brought me some tablets. Even after taking them, I didn't feel better. To put it simply, I couldn't even pick up my toothbrush to brush my teeth. I was exhausted,” the actress recalled.Actress visits hospital before reaching the setAccording to Mirnaa Menon, finding medical assistance proved difficult that morning. She said she visited several hospitals but could not find an available doctor. Eventually, she managed to get a doctor to attend to her after requesting urgent assistance.“But at that time, there were no doctors available at any of the hospitals. We went to four or five hospitals, but couldn't find a doctor. Finally, we reached one hospital and asked the doctor to come in urgently. We waited for him. I was thinking, ‘Isn't there anyone who can save me?’ That was how I felt,” she said.The doctor eventually administered an injection and provided another tablet for her symptoms. Since an important scene was scheduled, Mirnaa Menon took the additional medication while travelling to the shooting location.High-dose injection left Mirnaa Menon feeling numbMirnaa Menon described how the medication affected her while she was filming. She said her body felt numb and she became dehydrated. Her face also appeared swollen, although she felt the change in her appearance suited the scene.“That morning, I took a tablet on an empty stomach. Then I got the injection, followed by another tablet. By then, my body felt almost numb. Even if someone had hit me, I wouldn't have felt the pain. I also became dehydrated, and my face became swollen. However, that appearance worked for the scene, so my look wasn't a problem,” she said.The actress explained that her main concern was her performance. She felt she could not access the emotions required for the scene, which made her question whether she had delivered the expected result.Nelson Dilipkumar reassured the actress about her performanceMirnaa Menon said director Nelson Dilipkumar usually did not require her to perform more than two takes. However, she felt uncertain about the scene and requested another take to ensure it was right.“But I couldn't feel my emotions. Nelson sir usually doesn't make me do more than two takes. After this scene, I started wondering whether I had performed it properly,” she recalled.She added, “So, I suggested doing a third take. Nelson sir said it was fine. I told him that I felt I hadn't got it right. He reassured me that it was okay. I asked him whether it was absolutely fine, whether it was 100 per cent okay. He said everything was correct and there was no problem.”Although the director approved the scene, the experience continued to trouble her. She later watched the footage during dubbing and did not notice anything wrong with her performance.'Jailer 2' brings back Rajinikanth as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian'Jailer 2' sees Rajinikanth reprise his role as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, the retired jailer introduced in the 2023 movie 'Jailer'. The sequel continues the story involving the criminal network connected to Vinayakan's antagonist, whose dialogue in the first film hinted at a larger organisation operating behind him.Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa Menon and Rithvik return from the original cast. The new additions include S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu, Vidya Balan, Anna Rajan, Kottayam Nazeer and Jatin Sarna. articles.title: ‘Drishyam 3’: Shriya Saran reacts to 8-year age gap with on-screen daughter Ishita Dutta, says, 'Story impactful, all these things doesn't matter'
articles.summary: Shriya Saran is enjoying the success of ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’, in which she returns as Nandini Salgaonkar under Abhishek Pathak’s direction.
articles.body: Shriya Saran is enjoying the success of ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’, in which she returns as Nandini Salgaonkar under Abhishek Pathak’s direction. Ever since the franchise began, she has played the mother of Ishita Dutta’s character, even though Ishita is just eight years younger in real life. Ishita plays Anju Salgaonkar. The third instalment, led by Ajay Devgn, is currently running in theatres. In a recent interview, Shriya spoke about playing a mother to an actress who is only eight years her junior.Drishyam 3’s Shriya Saran says age gap “doesn’t make sense”Talking to News18, Shriya opened up about playing Ishita’s mother in the ‘Drishyam’ franchise. The actress said, “Yeah, I mean, it doesn’t make sense. I did think about it. I was like, how does it make any connect? I had to be a child to give birth to another child (laughs). But the story is so impactful and strong that you don’t think about all these things.”Shriya Saran on typecasting and Anju’s adoption in ‘Drishyam’The actress acknowledged that the film industry often typecasts women actors, but she praised the ‘Drishyam’ makers for justifying the age gap so well. She revealed that Ishita’s character, Anju, is an adopted child in the franchise, and said this has been explained beautifully. As the conversation went on, she also spoke about working with Ishita and how their personal equation has changed over time.“When we began working on Drishyam, we were both literally children! By the time we shot for Drishyam 2, she had just gotten married and I remember us speaking a lot about life. By the third film, we were discussing children,” she said. Shriya added that Ishita’s son Vayu is nearly the same age as her daughter Radha, so the two actresses mostly end up talking about classes. She also described her co-star as a “wonderful mother.”‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ box office collection‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’ arrived in theatres on October 2 with a bumper opening of Rs 62 crore. articles.title: 'Shah Rukh Khan Sir felt that the voice suited him': Abhay Jodhpurkar recalls how Ajay-Atul, Aanand L. Rai and Irshad Kamil 'took a stand' for him for ‘Mere Naam Tu’ song from 'Zero' amid pressure to replace him with an established singer
articles.summary: Singer Abhay Jodhpurkar’s National Award win for ‘Navasachi Gauri Mazi’ from ‘Gharat Ganpati’ marks a significant milestone in a career shaped by
articles.body: Singer Abhay Jodhpurkar’s National Award win for ‘Navasachi Gauri Mazi’ from ‘Gharat Ganpati’ marks a significant milestone in a career shaped by persistence, self-doubt and the challenges of breaking into the Hindi film music industry. In an interview with Variety India, the singer opened up about how his journey to lending his voice to Shah Rukh Khan in ‘Mere Naam Tu’ from ‘Zero’ was far from straightforward. He recalled how several of his recordings were replaced by established singers, how A.R. Rahman repeatedly tried to give him opportunities, and how composers Ajay-Atul stood their ground when his voice came under scrutiny.Abhay Jodhpurkar says A.R. Rahman tried to launch him in several projectsAbhay Jodhpurkar’s association with A.R. Rahman began with ‘Godfather’ in 2012. However, despite the composer’s efforts to introduce him to larger projects, several opportunities did not translate into songs that eventually made it to the screen.“Right after being launched by A.R. Rahman Sir with ‘Godfather’ in 2012, he has been trying to launch me in a lot of projects,” Jodhpurkar told Variety India.He recalled that his recordings for several films were eventually replaced by more established voices. “From ‘Jab Tak Hai Jaan’ to ‘Kochadaiiyaan’ to a lot of films that I had done a few scratches for, ended up with me being replaced by Arijit Singh or Sonu ji or other big names,” he said.Although he had already sung more than 100 songs in the South Indian film industry, establishing himself in Hindi cinema proved difficult.“I was still a beginner down south and had done over 100 songs... Sir tried to launch me, but then, it somehow was not working out,” he recalled.The repeated setbacks began affecting his confidence. “It has somehow never worked out. And I was also losing my morale. I was like, maybe it's something in me that I need to work on or I was having self-doubt,” he said.How Abhay Jodhpurkar became Shah Rukh Khan’s voice in ‘Mere Naam Tu’A turning point came after Jodhpurkar moved to Bombay and met composer duo Ajay-Atul. They were familiar with his work, including ‘Moongil Thottam’ and his cover of ‘Jeev Rangla’ from ‘Jogwa’, and invited him to record some of their material. One of those recordings became ‘Mere Naam Tu’, the romantic track from Shah Rukh Khan’s 2018 film ‘Zero’.“What was supposed to be just a trial, just a prep” eventually turned into a defining opportunity for the singer. The song was shot over 14 days, and the team was happy with how his voice complemented the actor.“Because after the recording, the song went on to be shot for 14 days and Shah Rukh Khan sir felt that the voice suited him. Aanand L. Rai Sir, Irshad Kamil Sir, were all very happy with it,” Jodhpurkar said.However, the positive response from the creative team did not immediately eliminate concerns about having a relatively unfamiliar singer front a major Hindi film song.‘There’s a huge risk’: Singer recalls pressure to replace him on ‘Mere Naam Tu’Jodhpurkar explained that ‘Mere Naam Tu’ was one of the biggest songs in ‘Zero’, making his selection a commercial risk in the eyes of some industry stakeholders. As an unfamiliar name in Hindi cinema, he faced the possibility of being replaced by a singer with an established audience.“It was the biggest song of the film. And you're betting it with a singer who is completely unknown to the Hindi industry,” he said. “So of course, there's a huge risk. And there's a lot of debate around that and pressure from the labels to ‘let's have a big singer sing it.’”This time, however, the people backing the song refused to give in to that pressure.“They stood up and they were like, ‘No, everyone has liked it and we won't let it be replaced because he’s done a good job and we feel like it should be retained,’” he recalled.Jodhpurkar believes that decision changed the course of his career. “Had they not taken that stand for me, I would have probably not been here now,” he said, adding, “It takes a lot of guts to do that.”Abhay Jodhpurkar criticises industry gatekeeping and commercial decision-makingHis experience with ‘Mere Naam Tu’ has shaped his views on the larger Hindi film music industry. Jodhpurkar believes that even when composers support a singer, commercial considerations can lead decision-makers to favour voices that are already popular.He cited his experience with Pritam, who, according to the singer, had recommended him for several projects.“Pritam Da has pitched me to so many projects and he has insisted that we should really clean up his version but somehow they feel like ‘this won't work, we need more energy, we need accents, we need a sick voice’... popular voices,” he said.For Jodhpurkar, the underlying problem is the lack of creative authority afforded to composers and artists when commercial decisions are made by producers and other stakeholders.“People who lack creativity or who don't understand musicality are taking calls for the thing because they are the producers,” he said. “So I think that is the biggest challenge when the composer or the artist are not respected for their talent and are just treated like slaves just because they are being employed by them.”Abhay Jodhpurkar’s National Award win for ‘Navasachi Gauri Mazi’Abhay Jodhpurkar clinched the Best Male Playback Singer honor at the 72nd National Film Awards for his soulful rendition of the song "Navasachi Gauri Mazi" from the Marathi family drama film 'Gharat Ganpati'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
